stories.title: Recall push targets Springfield Twp supervisor over data center fights
stories.dek: Residents are gathering signatures to oust the supervisor they blame for fast-tracking data center projects that could strain local roads, power and water. The effort shows how data center fights are now shaping township politics in southeast Michigan. A successful recall would shift control of future approvals.
stories.source_title: Springfield Township Supervisor Ric Davis targeted for recall - MLive.com

stories.title: Ypsilanti keeps data center freeze in place as residents demand more time
stories.dek: City council is extending the moratorium on new data centers while it studies power and water impacts. The pause blocks any large projects from moving forward in the near term. Residents 30 miles away in Ann Arbor and beyond could see ripple effects on regional electricity rates if big facilities get approved later.
stories.source_title: Ypsilanti City Council continues data center moratorium discussion - The Eastern Echo

stories.title: Developer restarts bid to turn old electric plant site into power-hungry facility
stories.dek: A developer is restarting efforts to build a data center at the old Emerson Electric campus. The project would bring new power demand and tax revenue questions to the local community. Residents nearby will feel the impact on electricity rates and land use.
stories.source_title: Ferguson revives push for data center at former Emerson campus - FOX 2

stories.title: Mason County breaks ground on two major data centers
stories.dek: Western Mason County has approved construction of two large-scale data centers. The projects will draw significant electricity from the regional grid and create construction and operations jobs. Local residents will see impacts on power reliability and tax revenue.
stories.source_title: Two high-impact data centers officially underway in western Mason County - DC News Now

stories.title: Kalamazoo adds moratorium to zoning code to slow data center rush
stories.dek: Kalamazoo officials are writing a temporary ban on new data centers into local rules as AI-driven proposals multiply. Residents could see fewer projects competing for power and land while the township studies impacts. The move comes amid statewide concerns over grid strain and water use from large facilities.
stories.source_title: Kalamazoo works to add data center moratorium to zoning code amid rapid growth of AI technology - FOX 17 West Michigan News

stories.title: Garfield Twp to spend a year crafting data center rules
stories.dek: Garfield Township supervisors will take 12 months to draft zoning and permitting standards for data centers. Residents in Grand Traverse County could see limits on power demand, noise, and water use before any project advances. The delay gives locals time to weigh impacts on taxes, traffic, and the local grid.
stories.source_title: Garfield Township plans on spending a year deciding how to regulate data centers - 9and10News.com

stories.title: Mid-Michigan residents get first look at data center power and water demands
stories.dek: A university-hosted town hall will lay out how proposed data centers could affect local electricity rates and aquifer levels. Residents within 30 miles will hear concrete numbers on megawatts and daily water use. The session gives nearby communities a chance to question developers before projects advance.
stories.source_title: Data center town hall scheduled at mid-Michigan university - MLive.com

stories.title: Lakeshore township blocks data centers using existing zoning rules
stories.dek: Officials say current ordinances already prevent large-scale server farms from locating near homes and wells. The decision keeps water and noise impacts off the table for now. Nearby west Michigan towns are watching to see if the same language works for them.
stories.source_title: Lakeshore town leans on current rules to keep out data centers - MLive.com

stories.title: Ypsilanti-area residents plan protest over data center water use
stories.dek: Activists will gather at the Van Buren Township line to oppose projects they say threaten local wells and raise power costs. The Saturday event targets two proposed campuses that could draw millions of gallons daily. Washtenaw and Wayne county homeowners within driving distance have a direct stake.
stories.source_title: Data center protesters to gather Saturday at Ypsilanti, Van Buren Township line - MLive.com

stories.title: Farm seeks city annexation to build Michigan data center
stories.dek: A rural property owner is pushing to join a nearby city so a data center can be built on farmland. The move would shift tax revenue and local control away from the township. Residents 30 miles away will feel the change in land use and services if the annexation succeeds.
stories.source_title: A farm wants a data center in rural Michigan — and it has to join a city to do it - Crain's Detroit

stories.title: U-M computing center raises nuclear weapons worries
stories.dek: University of Michigan plans for a new computing facility are drawing fire over possible ties to nuclear weapons work. Ann Arbor residents and activists want clearer answers on how the project could support military programs. The debate affects state research funding and local oversight of university expansion.
stories.source_title: U-M’s proposed computing center draws concerns over role in nuclear weapons modernization - Michigan Advance

national.title: Data centers advance rapidly as regulators scramble for rules
national.dek: Across the U.S., officials race to impose guardrails on power-hungry facilities while communities push back on incentives and impacts.
